Calculate the discriminant to see if solutions exist. If positive, two real roots; if zero, one root; if negative, complex roots. Always verify by substituting back.

Differentiate f(x) to get f'(x). Set f'(x) = 0 and solve for x. These x-values are candidates for stationary points. Plug them back into f(x) to find the y-values. Then, use the second derivative test: if f''(x) > 0, it’s a local minimum; if < 0, a local maximum.
